en.L01: Reference ranges in a PDF. Formulas in a chat. A calculator in another app.
en.L02: Laboratory knowledge, scattered — and rarely in your own language.
en.L03: LabGuide brings it together: a laboratory reference and learning app in Uzbek, Russian and English.
en.L04: Core content works offline and without an account — with no ads and no tracking.
en.L05: Choose your role, and the home screen follows.
en.L06: For the laboratory specialist: answers at the bench.
en.L07: Test cards give units, guideline thresholds and what high or low results can mean — with the source behind each claim.
en.L08: Calculators work only from your own values, and show the formula, limits and sources.
en.L09: Quality control: Levey–Jennings charts, with Westgard rules applied to every run.
en.L10: Record a calibration. Count a differential, with percentages and absolute counts.
en.L11: Browse the instrument catalog and the atlases.
en.L12: Specialists can also practise for the qualification category assessment.
en.L13: And your records stay on your phone.
en.L14: For the teacher: lecture slides and practical protocols, ready for a big screen — offline too.
en.L15: Open a class: students join with a QR code or a short code.
en.L16: Set a lecture test — questions can differ per student.
en.L17: Then see the results by student, and the hardest questions.
en.L18: For the student: learn from slides, topic by topic, then check yourself.
en.L19: Five new questions every day, and topic quizzes where every answer is explained.
en.L20: Timed practice exams work offline, and mistakes can be practised again.
en.L21: When your teacher sets a test, it waits on your home screen.
en.L22: One app for specialist, teacher and student.
en.L23: LabGuide. A reference and learning aid — it does not diagnose.

en.L02: Without a calibration, nobody can say.
en.L03: In the analyzer, light passes through the reaction cuvette; the photometer measures absorbance.
en.L04: The concentration is then calculated from a calibration.
en.L05: More light absorbed means less reaches the detector — and a higher absorbance.
en.L06: Calibrators have assigned values; each level gives one signal.
en.L07: Plot absorbance against concentration, point by point.
en.L08: A least-squares line through the points is the calibration curve.
en.L09: Slope, intercept and R² are computed from these points.
en.L10: A control with a known target is read off the curve.
en.L11: R² alone is not enough: residuals should be small, with no trend.
en.L12: Acceptance limits come from your IFU and SOP.
en.L13: LabGuide doesn’t calibrate the analyzer — it records how calibration was done.
en.L14: Instrument, analyte, reagent REF, IFU revision — and no guessed parameters.
en.L15: Then the record: calibrator lot, assigned values, unit — from the value sheet.
en.L16: “Accepted” is blocked until QC after calibration has passed…
en.L17: …and until an authorized person is named.
en.L18: Saved records go to the calibration log — on this device.
en.L19: Create, edit, delete — each leaves a history entry, even after deletion.
en.L20: Calibration is not just a curve. It’s confidence in every result.

uz.L03: Levey–Jennings grafigi har nazorat natijasini o‘rtacha va SD bilan solishtiradi.
uz.L05: Har natija — z: o‘rtachadan necha SD uzoqda.
uz.L06: 2 SD dan tashqari bitta qiymat — 1-2s: ogohlantirish, rad emas.
uz.L08: 1-3s va R-4s — tasodifiy xato: seriya rad etiladi.
uz.L10: Bu yerda ketma-ket to‘rt qiymat 1 SD dan tashqarida: 4-1s. Rad, sababini toping.
uz.L11: LabGuide’da har daraja uchun o‘rtacha va SD hamda ularning manbai kiritiladi.
uz.L12: Har seriyani yozing — grafikni ilova chizadi.
uz.L13: Westgard qoidalari har seriyada tekshiriladi, qoida nomlanadi.
uz.L14: Rad etilgan seriya tarixda qoladi, hisobga kirmaydi.
uz.L15: CSV jadval nusxasi — ma’lumot faqat shu qurilmada.

en.L01: This morning’s control: 2.3 SD above the mean.
en.L02: Stop the run — or report the patients?
en.L03: A Levey–Jennings chart plots every control result against its target mean and SD.
en.L04: Targets come from your own control data: about twenty values to start.
en.L05: Each result becomes a z-score: how many SDs it sits from the mean.
en.L06: One value beyond 2 SD is the 1-2s rule: a warning, not a rejection.
en.L07: Inspect it with the other rules first.
en.L08: 1-3s and R-4s point to random error: reject the run.
en.L09: 2-2s, 4-1s and 10x point to systematic error — a shift.
en.L10: Here, four values in a row beyond 1 SD: 4-1s. Reject, and find the cause.
en.L11: In LabGuide, enter each level’s target mean and SD — and where they came from.
en.L12: Record every run; the app draws the Levey–Jennings chart.
en.L13: Westgard rules are checked on every run, and the broken rule is named.
en.L14: A rejected run stays in the history, but is not used in later rules or statistics.
en.L15: Copy the runs as a table — data stays on this device.
en.L16: A control result is a decision, not just a dot.

uz.L03: Fotometr kyuvetadan bir to‘lqin uzunlikdagi nur o‘tkazadi.
uz.L04: Optik zichlik — kirgan va chiqqan nur nisbati: A = log₁₀(I₀/I).
uz.L05: A = 1 da nurning faqat 10 % i o‘tadi, A = 2 da — 1 % i.
uz.L06: Ma’lum oraliqda optik zichlik konsentratsiyaga mutanosib: bu Buger–Lambert–Ber qonuni.
uz.L07: Chegaradan oshsa, egri chiziq bukiladi va natija past chiqadi.
uz.L08: Uch kyuveta: blank nolni qo‘yadi, so‘ng standart va namuna.
uz.L09: C = A namuna ÷ A standart × standart konsentratsiyasi.
uz.L10: Chegaradan oshsa: suyultiring, qayta o‘lchang, ko‘paytiring.
uz.L11: LabGuide: ma’ruza rejimida fotometriya protokoli bor.
uz.L12: Blank, standart va namuna — bosqichma-bosqich, hisoblash ham…
uz.L14: To‘lqin uzunligi, blank va chegaralar — reagent IFU’sidan.
uz.L15: LabGuide — O‘rganish → Ma’ruza rejimi → Amaliy protokollar.

en.L03: A photometer shines one wavelength through the cuvette.
en.L04: Absorbance compares the light going in with the light coming out: A = log₁₀(I₀/I).
en.L05: At absorbance 1, only ten percent of the light gets through; at 2, one percent.
en.L06: Within a range, absorbance rises in proportion to concentration: the Beer–Lambert law.
en.L07: Past the linearity limit, the curve bends: readings fall short.
en.L08: Three cuvettes: the blank sets zero, then standard, then sample.
en.L09: Concentration = A sample ÷ A standard × C standard.
en.L10: Above the limit? Dilute, measure again, and multiply by the dilution factor.
en.L11: LabGuide’s Lecture mode has a protocol on photometry basics.
en.L12: Blank, standard and sample, step by step — and the calculation…
en.L13: …plus the rule for results above the linearity limit.
en.L14: Wavelength, blank and limits always come from your reagent’s IFU.
en.L15: LabGuide — Learn → Lecture mode → Practical protocols.

en.L01: Two samples freeze — and one plateau sits lower. Why?
en.L02: Dissolved particles lower the freezing point. That is what an osmometer measures.
en.L03: A freezing-point osmometer: sample tubes, a thermistor probe, a cooling block, a stirring wire and a display.
en.L04: The cooling block supercools the sample below its freezing point.
en.L05: The stirring wire vibrates, and freezing starts.
en.L06: Released heat lifts the temperature to a plateau: the freezing point.
en.L07: More particles, a deeper depression — and from it, the osmolality.
en.L08: Osmolality is per kilogram of water, in mOsm/kg; osmolarity is per litre of solution.
en.L09: In LabGuide: Lab → Instruments and methods → Clinical biochemistry → Osmometer.
en.L10: The same schematic and parts, plus specimens — each with its source.
en.L11: Particles, air bubbles, evaporated or viscous samples, and high alcohol or acetone distort the reading.
en.L12: And an uncleaned container carries the last sample into the next.
en.L13: Lab → Calculators → Calculated osmolality: from sodium, glucose and urea.
en.L14: Add the measured value, and it shows the osmolal gap.
en.L15: Measured or calculated — know which number you read.
en.L16: LabGuide — Lab → Instruments and methods → Osmometer.

uz.L04: Eritrotsit tegib, ustma-ust tushmagan joyda sanang.

uz.L09: Limfotsit: yumaloq zich yadro, ingichka ko‘k hoshiya.
uz.L11: Maydonma-maydon, bir tomonga, orqaga qaytmay — hujayra ikki marta sanalmasin.
uz.L12: Har uchragan leykotsitni turiga ajrating — 100 tagacha.
uz.L13: LabGuide’da har hujayra turining o‘z katta tugmasi bor.
uz.L15: Jami va har bir foiz har bosishda yangilanadi.
uz.L16: 100 yoki 200 hujayra. Maqsadga yetganda sanash to‘xtaydi…
uz.L18: Mikroskop rejimi: katta zonalar — ko‘z okulyardan uzilmaydi.
uz.L19: Har turning o‘z tebranishi bor; har 10-hujayrada — uzun signal.
uz.L20: Foiz = son ÷ jami. WBC bilan: mutlaq son = ulush × WBC.

en.L02: On paper, a hundred-cell differential is easy to lose.
en.L03: Under the oil objective, a stained blood film: red cells, platelets — and white cells.
en.L04: Count where red cells touch but don’t overlap.
en.L05: Segmented neutrophil: two to five lobes joined by thin strands, pale pink cytoplasm.
en.L06: Band neutrophil: one curved nucleus, not divided into lobes.
en.L07: Eosinophil: usually two lobes, packed with large orange-red granules.
en.L08: Basophil: large, deep purple granules that cover the nucleus.
en.L09: Lymphocyte: a round, dense nucleus with a thin blue rim.
en.L10: Monocyte: the largest — a folded, kidney-shaped nucleus in grey-blue cytoplasm.
en.L11: Move field by field in one direction, never back, so no cell is counted twice.
en.L12: Classify each white cell as you meet it, until you reach 100.
en.L13: In LabGuide, every cell class has its own big button.
en.L14: One tap adds one to that cell; a long press takes one away.
en.L15: The total and every percentage update with each tap.
en.L16: Choose 100 or 200 cells. At the target, counting stops…
en.L17: …and an extra tap is not added.
en.L18: Microscope mode: big screen zones, so your eyes stay on the eyepiece.
en.L19: Each cell type has its own vibration pattern; every tenth cell, a longer signal.
en.L20: Percent is count over total. With the WBC, absolute count is fraction times WBC.
en.L21: Enter the WBC, and absolute counts appear next to each percentage.
en.L22: Reference ranges come from your lab’s report form — and the comparison is not a diagnosis.
en.L23: Save the result on this device, or copy it as text.
en.L24: Keep your eyes on the cells. LabGuide keeps the count.

en.L04: Seventeen of them: clinical formulas, manual methods and laboratory tools.

en.L10: Under 18, eGFR is refused: the equation was built on adults.

en.L12: SI or conventional units: chosen once, in Profile.
en.L13: Bench tools too: dilution, C1·V1 = C2·V2, from your own numbers.

uz.L01: Noma’lum namunada uch cho‘qqi. Qaysi biri qaysi modda?
uz.L02: GC-MS avval ularni ajratadi, so‘ng bo‘laklarini o‘qiydi.
uz.L03: Gaz xromatografi: tashuvchi gaz, avtonamunaoluvchi, injektor. So‘ng kolonkali termostat va uzatish liniyasi.
uz.L04: Moddalar kolonkadan turli vaqtda chiqadi — bu ushlanish vaqti.
uz.L05: GC uchun modda uchuvchan bo‘lsin, ba’zan derivatizatsiya bilan.
uz.L06: So‘ng mass-spektrometr: ion manbai, kvadrupol, detektor, vakuum nasoslari va ma’lumotlar tizimi.
uz.L08: Kvadrupol ionlarni massa/zaryad nisbati — m/z bo‘yicha saralab, navbat bilan o‘tkazadi.
uz.L09: Natija: ushlanish vaqti bo‘yicha xromatogramma va har cho‘qqining mass-spektri.
uz.L10: Modda spektrlar kutubxonasi yoki standartlar bilan aniqlanadi.
uz.L11: QC bo‘lmasa, spektrda begona cho‘qqilar chiqishi mumkin.
uz.L12: LabGuide’da: Lab → Apparatlar va metodikalar → Toksikologiya → GC-MS kartasi.
uz.L13: Sxema, qismlar, tamoyil va vazifalar — har biri manbali.
uz.L14: Kartada sifat nazorati va biologik xavfsizlik ham bor: issiq qismlar, ko‘zoynak, xalat, qo‘lqop.
uz.L16: LabGuide — Lab → Apparatlar va metodikalar → GC-MS.

en.L01: Three peaks in one unknown sample. Which compound is which?
en.L02: GC-MS separates them first, then reads their fragments.
en.L03: The gas chromatograph: carrier gas, autosampler, heated injector, an oven with a capillary column, and a heated transfer line.
en.L04: Compounds leave the column at different times: the retention time.
en.L05: For GC, the analyte must be volatile — sometimes after derivatization.
en.L06: Then the mass spectrometer: ion source, quadrupole, detector, vacuum pumps and data system.
en.L07: Molecules are ionised and break into fragment ions.
en.L08: The quadrupole sorts ions by mass-to-charge ratio, m/z, and passes them in turn.
en.L09: The result: a chromatogram over retention time, and a mass spectrum for every peak.
en.L10: Compounds are identified against a spectral library or standards.
en.L11: Without quality control, peaks that don’t belong to the sample can appear.
en.L12: In LabGuide: Lab → Instruments and methods → Toxicology → the GC-MS card.
en.L13: The same schematic and parts, then principle and tasks — each sourced.
en.L14: QC notes and biosafety are on the card too: hot parts, glasses, coat and gloves.
en.L15: From peak to identity — one step at a time.
en.L16: LabGuide — Lab → Instruments and methods → GC-MS.

uz.L01: A namuna chiziqni 22-siklda, B namuna 31-siklda kesib o‘tadi.
uz.L02: Qaysi birida boshida nishon ko‘proq edi?
uz.L03: Har siklda qizdirish zanjirlarni ajratadi; sovutishda praymerlar birikadi, polimeraza yangi zanjir quradi.
uz.L04: Nishon har siklda qariyb ikki barobar ko‘payadi.
uz.L05: Termosiklator: probirkalar qatori, isitiladigan qopqoq va Peltye termobloki.
uz.L06: Har siklda qo‘zg‘atuvchi nur filtr orqali probirkaga tushadi.
uz.L07: Bo‘yoq fluoressensiyasi nurlanish filtridan detektorga o‘tadi.
uz.L08: Signal mahsulot bilan o‘sadi — kuchayish egri chizig‘i.
uz.L09: Cq — chegara kesib o‘tilgan sikl: Cq qancha past bo‘lsa, boshida nishon shuncha ko‘p.
uz.L10: Ozgina ifloslanish soxta natija beradi, kuchayish yo‘qligi esa manfiylikni isbotlamaydi.
uz.L11: LabGuide’da: Lab → Apparatlar va metodikalar, so‘ng Molekulyar diagnostika → Real vaqt PCR.

en.L01: Sample A crosses the line at cycle 22, sample B at 31.
en.L02: Which one had more target to begin with?
en.L03: Each cycle, heat separates the strands; on cooling, primers bind and a polymerase builds new strands.
en.L04: So the target roughly doubles every cycle.
en.L05: The thermal cycler: tube strip, heated lid, and a Peltier block that switches temperatures.
en.L06: Every cycle, the excitation source shines through the excitation filter into the tube.
en.L07: The dye’s fluorescence passes the emission filter to the detector.
en.L08: Fluorescence grows with the product: the amplification curve.
en.L09: Cq is the cycle where it crosses the threshold — the lower the Cq, the more starting target.
en.L10: Trace contamination can give false results, and no amplification does not prove a negative.
en.L11: In LabGuide: Lab → Instruments and methods → Molecular diagnostics → Real-time PCR.
en.L12: This schematic, its numbered parts, and the principle — with sources.
en.L13: Limitations and contamination control are on the card too.
en.L14: Read the curve, not just the Cq.
en.L15: LabGuide — Lab → Instruments and methods → Real-time PCR.
